newsitem.title: GREECE: BASKETBALL-BESIKTAS' US PLAYER CHARGED AFTER FIGHT.
newsitem.headline: BASKETBALL-BESIKTAS' US PLAYER CHARGED AFTER FIGHT.

text.p: Turkish Besiktas's American forward Gary Alexander was arrested and charged on Thursday over a brawl that interrupted a Korac Cup basketball match with Greece's Aris, police said.
A public prosecutor in this northern Greek city charged Alexander with assault and freed him pending trial.
Police said they arrested Alexander at his hotel hours before his team was scheduled to fly to Turkey after a suit was filed by Aris forward Dinos Angelidis.
Television showed Alexander hitting Angelidis from behind and then grabbing him and throwing him out of the court. Other players quickly joined in the brawl and the game was abandoned.
Aris was leading 40-31 a minute and a half into the second half when the violence errupted. Police moved in to tear the fighting players apart.

The Turkish team demanded that a banner hoisted by Greek fans, reading "Greece's capital is Constantinople", be taken down but referees and FIBA officials said they had no juristiction outside the court.
Most Greeks refer to the modern Turkish city of Istanbul as Constantinople, the city's Byzantine name.
Aris officials said the banner was in response to a banner put up by Turkish fans in the first leg game in Istanbul, which read "Cyprus is Turkish".
Greece and Turkey have long been at odds over several issues, including the divided island of Cyprus, rights in the Aegean Sea and minority rights in both countries.
